findings.quote: saying that he would somehow make Gentius well disposed
findings.problem: Greek has a lacuna: φάσκων ἐξιγμένον *** εὐνοοῦντα ποιήσειν τὸν Γένθιον. English smooths it with an invented 'somehow'.
findings.proposed_fix: saying that [...] he would make Gentius well disposed

findings.problem: πάντας ἂν συνέβη ... τοὺς πλείστους ἐξελεγχθῆναι: ἐξελέγχω means to be tested/exposed/shown up, not 'won over'. Greek does not say they would be won over.
findings.proposed_fix: would have been put to the proof

findings.quote: by good fortune he did not take that path
findings.problem: νῦν δὲ καλῶς ποιῶν οὐκ ἦλθε ταύτην τὴν ὁδόν: 'doing well / acting rightly', not 'by good fortune' (no τύχη here).
findings.proposed_fix: he did well not to take that path

findings.quote: only a very few Greeks were driven into utter folly at the crisis of the action
findings.problem: δι᾽ ἧς ὀλίγοι τελέως ἠλογήθησαν τῶν Ἑλλήνων ὑπὸ τὸν τῆς πράξεως καιρόν: ἀλογέω = to disregard/neglect; 'few were utterly disregarded'. No 'folly'.
findings.proposed_fix: by which few of the Greeks were utterly disregarded at the time of the action

units.note: Sentence ending 'ἠλογήθησαν' is somewhat compressed/possibly corrupt; fix keeps the plain sense. Lacunae also at end of 'δυνάμενοι πράττειν *' and before '** ὅτι γάρ' (English does not mark them).

findings.quote: King Ptolemy had applied to the Achaeans because the customary rites performed for kings when they come of age had now taken place in his case
findings.problem: περὶ τοῦ βασιλέως Πτολεμαίου προσπεσόντος τοῖς Ἀχαιοῖς διότι γέγονεν αὐτῷ τὰ νομιζόμενα...ἀνακλητήρια: προσπίπτω = news reached; the Achaeans received word, Ptolemy did not apply to them. διότι is 'that', not 'because'.
findings.proposed_fix: word reached the Achaeans concerning King Ptolemy that the customary ceremonies (the anaklētēria) performed for kings when they come of age had now taken place in his case

findings.quote: his fellow envoys were to send word back at once explaining this
findings.problem: τοὺς μὲν συμπρεσβευτὰς ἐξ αὐτῆς πέμπειν διασαφήσοντας: Polybius is to send his colleagues off at once to report; the colleagues are the object, not the subject.
findings.proposed_fix: he was to send his fellow envoys off at once to report this

findings.quote: decide the whole issue by force of arms
findings.problem: λήψεσθαι τὰ ὅλα κρίσιν ἐκ τῶν κατὰ λόγον: 'the whole matter would be decided, as was to be expected / in the natural course'; no mention of arms. Phrase possibly corrupt.
findings.proposed_fix: decide the whole issue, as was to be expected

findings.problem: Ἀλκίθον is accusative of Ἀλκίθος (cf. Ch. 19 Ἀλκίθος); name should be Alcithus.

units.note: Talents are τάλαντα μεγάλα (omitted 'large' qualifier; not treated as error).

findings.quote: Agesilochus son of Hegesias was sent to Rome, along with Nicagoras son of Nicander
findings.problem: Ἁγησίλοχος Ἁγησίου, Νικαγόρας, Νίκανδρος: three separate envoys (Nicander is a man, not Nicagoras' father); English drops one envoy.
findings.proposed_fix: Agesilochus son of Hegesias, Nicagoras and Nicander were sent to Rome

units.note: Text has a visible gap after Ἁγησίου, possibly a lost name; the three-name reading is what the Greek states.
